ledger.note: 1415: Frederick of Hohenzollern is made Margrave and Elector of Brandenburg. 'Sigismund granted him the titles at the Council of Constance on 30 April 1415' and 'the king awarded him the formal enfeoffment of the margraviate on 18 April 1417' (Frederick I page); he had been 'Oberster Hauptmann und Verwalter der Marken (1411)'. This is the Margraviate of Brandenburg (electorate since 25 December 1356, Margraviate page) under a new dynasty, the Hohenzollern; Cliopatria splits it into a Margraviate row to 1414 and an Electorate row from 1422.

1417: Berlin becomes the capital. Infobox 'Capital: Brandenburg an der Havel (1157-1417), then Berlin (1417-1806)'; 'Berlin became the residence that year' (Margraviate page). The Frederick I page has the Landtag asking him to rule from Berlin on 21 October 1415.

1445: Brandenburg acquires Cottbus from Bohemia. 'In 1445 Cottbus was acquired by the Margraviate of Brandenburg from Bohemia'; it was 'an exclave almost completely surrounded by Bohemian Lower Lusatia'. The radius is the researcher's; Cliopatria never draws Cottbus.

region.text: the Neumark east of the Oder

ledger.note: 1455: the Neumark returns to Brandenburg. 'In 1454 and 1455, he concluded the Treaties of Cölln and Mewe and thereby re-gained the Neumark (New March) from the Teutonic Order state.' The Neumark page: pawned back in 1454/1455, 're-acquisition completed in 1463 for 40,000 guilders'; Cliopatria draws it from 1459.

region.text: the Duchy of Pomerania, brought under Brandenburg's supremacy

ledger.note: 1472: the Treaty of Prenzlau puts Pomerania under Brandenburg's supremacy. 'By the 1472 Treaty of Prenzlau' Albert Achilles ended the War of the Succession of Stettin, 'bringing the Duchy of Pomerania also under his supremacy'. The Margraviate page lists Prenzlau treaties of 1448, 1472 and 1479 that 'ended the wars with Pomerania'.

1529: Brandenburg gives up its overlordship of Pomerania. The Pomerania page says the Pomeranian dukes' imperial grant of 1348 'was not accepted by Brandenburg until 1529'; the year is the page's, that this ends the supremacy is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Neumark east of the Oder

ledger.note: 1535: the Neumark becomes Brandenburg-Küstrin. 'As Brandenburg-Küstrin the Neumark formed an independent state of the Holy Roman Empire from 1535 to 1571.' The administration moved from Soldin to Küstrin in 1548.

region.text: the Neumark east of the Oder

ledger.note: 1571: the Neumark is reunited with the Kurmark. 'The Neumark became reunited with the Kurmark under Joachim II's son, John George.'

region.text: Cleves, Mark and Ravensberg: the part of Brandenburg-Prussia's 1619 outline in North Rhine-Westphalia

ledger.note: 1609: Brandenburg claims the Jülich-Cleves inheritance. John William, Duke of Jülich-Cleves-Berg, dies on 25 March 1609 without heirs; 'Johann Sigismund of Brandenburg claimed the duchies through his wife' against Wolfgang Wilhelm of Neuburg, and the claimants 'signed the Treaty of Dortmund (1609)' on 10 June 1609. The page does not say which towns each held, so the zone is Brandenburg's later share.

notes: Scope: Cliopatria's Electorate row is 1422-1618 (13 shapes); this dossier runs 1415-1618 (the Margraviate row ends in 1414). It is the Hohenzollern phase of one state: Cliopatria's Margraviate of Brandenburg (1260-1414) and Electorate (1422-1618) share Wikidata Q148499 and the article 'Margraviate of Brandenburg' (electorate since 25 December 1356, Margraviate page). Under the brief they would be one dossier under the earlier slug; margraviate-of-brandenburg belongs to another batch, so this dossier is written on its own, with that slug as predecessor, and the orchestrator should merge or link them. Corrections applied to every shape: (1) the Franconian lands of the Hohenzollern (Ansbach, Kulmbach/Bayreuth) are taken out of 1422-1458, being a separate inheritance that Holy Roman Empire Minor States also draws; (2) the central and eastern Altmark (Stendal, Tangermünde, Gardelegen), which Cliopatria adds only in 1572, is added to 1415-1571; (3) the Neumark is added in 1455 and taken out in 1535-1570 for Brandenburg-Küstrin; (4) Cottbus (1445) is added; (5) Cleves, Mark and Ravensberg are added from 1614. The 1463 outline's two extra cells near Beeskow and Lieberose are unexplained. Not entered for lack of a page: Crossen (Brandenburg from 1482, not drawn by Cliopatria), the county of Ruppin (1524), Beeskow and Storkow, the Treaty of Brieg (1537), the Treaty of Grimnitz, Magdeburg and Halberstadt administration, and the dates of Albert Achilles' and John Cicero's reigns (1470/1471 and 1486 are only partly on the pages: Frederick II abdicated in 1470, Albert is elector from 1471). The pages give no ruler list for the Electorate, so none is entered. Counterparts that need dossiers: brandenburg-kustrin (the Neumark, 1535-1571), duchy-of-pomerania (1472-1529), julich-cleves-berg (to 1609) and palatinate-neuburg (the claimant of 1609-1614); teutonic-order and kingdom-of-bohemia exist. Gazetteer names wanted: Altmark, Neumark, Brandenburg an der Havel, Cleves, Mark (county), Ravensberg, Lower Lusatia. The Cliopatria area is 41-44 k km2 against the infobox's 26 k km2 for 1535 (ratio 0.61).
